articles.headline: Perplexity and Intelligence
articles.blurb: Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average. Lower perplexity means better predictions. Perplexity has stood the test of time as a metric many research teams have put a lot of effort into optimizing. It will likely play an important role in standardizing how AI progress is discussed as it continues to deliver consistent gains in general intelligence.

articles.headline: Inkling 2 Mini
articles.blurb: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B-parameter open-weight model that does extra internal computation to reason more before it answers. It leads every open-weight model under 100B parameters on the DeepSWE coding benchmark.

articles.headline: AI R&D-Relevant Model Capabilities Are Improving Rapidly
articles.blurb: Frontier AI models often match or beat skilled humans on well-defined coding and optimization tasks. The length of tasks they can complete doubles about every 3.6 months. METR says public evidence can't rule out a drastic speedup in AI research within the next couple of years.

articles.headline: The Most Important Charts in AI are Wrong
articles.blurb: AI capabilities are starting to become impressive. However, they are still dramatically inferior to what influential AI forecasts and benchmarks have predicted. These forecasts and benchmarks say that we are imminently close to reaching super-intelligence, but the gap between the real world and forecasts keeps growing larger. Now that real-world data exists, it's time to shift from being AI theorists to becoming AI empiricists.

articles.headline: Why Post-Training Could Teach Models to Evade Monitoring
articles.blurb: Penalizing detected reward hacking during post-training could select for behavior that evades monitors. The industry needs stronger training sandboxes, better-audited tasks and graders, and empirical research into whether interventions improve alignment or merely conceal undesirable behavior.

articles.headline: Tencent Releases Hy4 With Multimodal Input and Million-Token Context
articles.blurb: Tencent's open-weight Hy4 supports text, image, and video understanding with a 770-billion-parameter backbone activating 49 billion parameters per token. It combines million-token context, sparse attention, and a speculative-decoding drafter, targeting coding, computer use, finance, research, and long-running assistant workflows.

articles.headline: NVIDIA Releases Nemotron-Labs-Sigma Continuous Diffusion Language Models
articles.blurb: Nemotron-Labs-Sigma is a family of 14 open checkpoints at 3B and 8B that generate text by denoising compact token embeddings instead of predicting one token at a time. The 8B model supports few-step generation and self-speculative decoding, reaching a 3.46x average throughput speedup over autoregressive decoding on a GB200.

articles.headline: Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness to improve performance and cost
articles.blurb: Hugging Face has introduced harness adapters, allowing models like Qwen3.8-27B to optimize performance in specific harness-task combinations. By incorporating RL-trained LoRA adapters, the models achieve higher accuracy and efficiency, reducing token usage significantly.

articles.headline: The Brother-Sister Duo Who Want to Keep Anthropic Weird
articles.blurb: Anthropic embraces being atypical because it believes the artificial intelligence future will be anything but normal. Dario Amodei, 43, the company's chief executive, is Anthropic's ideological leader. He has one direct report, his chief of staff and sister, Daniela Amodei, 29. The company has made some unusual choices, and it screens out new hires with culture interviews. This article looks at the Amodeis and how they created a company culture in their likeness.

articles.headline: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis
articles.blurb: Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as a Lean library comprising 17 million lines of code on November 20. The Lean and Mathlib communities have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct. Alpöge's library compiles correctly, and the code proves the correct statement. It is expected that the mathematical community will help explain the ideas in the proof in the coming weeks.

articles.blurb: The release notes for Tesla's Full Self-Driving v15 read like a list of the feature's biggest current weaknesses. The update includes improvements to sign detection, potholes, and speed handling in school zones. It also adds an impressive-looking live visualization. FSD can now slow down for speed cameras. The update is currently being rolled out.

articles.headline: Anthropic Mathematician Says AI Has Solved the Most Famous Problem in Math
articles.blurb: An Anthropic researcher claims he worked with AI to discover a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. The conjecture in number theory predicts how primes are distributed. Mathematicians have been trying to crack it for 167 years, without success. The researcher's proof passed verification with proof-checking software.

articles.headline: The Merge
articles.blurb: Neuralink has increased the rate of surgeries and extended its clinical trials to Canada and the UK. The first participants in the company's studies now hold video chats with new participants to coach them on how to adjust to the technology. The terms of their trials don't include the option for upgrades. Unless Neuralink comes up with a commercial device, they will have to return to their pre-cyborg lives.

articles.headline: AI x Bio is not _just_ a data problem
articles.blurb: How far AI gets in biology will depend largely on how much data we have. It will also depend on what is measured and the quality of that data. An abundance of systematically incomplete measurements is unlikely to lead to a comprehensive understanding of many of the complex systems that occur in biology. AI will likely become a powerful tool that will contribute to the study of biology, but there is still no clear path to documenting a comprehensive account of how a whole cell or tissue works.

articles.headline: Vibecoding an inference chip
articles.blurb: AI allows developers to work in entirely new domains by giving them access to new programming languages and paradigms. This developer vibe-coded an FPGA into running an LLM. The article details the experience. The experiment shows what is now possible with a large token budget and interesting problems to point them at.

articles.headline: Informal Verification
articles.blurb: Verification is an exercise in building trust. A formal approach may be sufficient, but not necessary. This post explores the use of System One models as informal proof checkers. Informal methods can play a complementary role in establishing trust in agentic software engineering flows.

articles.headline: I don't expect superintelligence in 2027
articles.blurb: The industry seems to have a preference towards believing in extremely short timelines. We are probably about 60% of the way towards superintelligence relative to where we were in 2022. Superintelligence will likely arrive in 2029 rather than in 2027. While this seems like a tiny difference, it changes what the industry should prioritize. The current push towards deprioritizing 'long-timeline' work is not a good idea.

articles.headline: The Alice Huang Associate Accused of Funneling Nvidia Chips to China
articles.blurb: Li Ming, a 52-year-old Chinese national, was reportedly a central operator of a web of companies that smuggled restricted Nvidia AI chips to China. The web included Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company led by Alice Huang, with whom Jensen Huang had an affair. Li is currently out on bail in Singapore, living in a luxury villa down the street from the Chinese embassy. Li was charged with fraud in February 2025 in a case tied to the alleged transshipment of Nvidia chips. His criminal case is ongoing.

articles.blurb: Google is donating Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF to help run AI agents securely at scale. Agent Substrate separates agent state from compute in pre-warmed Kubernetes pools, which Google says lets agents resume in under 500 milliseconds.

articles.headline: Introducing in-place migration to GKE Dataplane V2
articles.blurb: Google Cloud released in-place migration to GKE Dataplane V2 in preview for VPC native clusters on GKE 1.35 or later. Teams can move from Dataplane V1 without building a parallel cluster, and they can roll back before finalization.

articles.headline: Karpenter v1.15: GPU-aware provisioning, smarter node repair, and more
articles.blurb: Karpenter v1.15 adds Dynamic Resource Allocation support to factor GPU topology and networking into provisioning decisions. It classifies node repair as a voluntary disruption that respects Pod Disruption Budgets. The update also introduces a pod deletion cost controller and CEL support for dynamic kubelet configurations.

articles.headline: Building PlanetScale with Insights Agent
articles.blurb: PlanetScale's database optimization agent added an index that made a production query slower because its SQL summary hid a 645-element IN list. Removing that list and filtering the small result set in Ruby cut average query time from 28.5 milliseconds to 1.95 milliseconds. Another change reordered a feature flag check, reducing database lookups from 28.7 million to 8.3 million per day.

articles.headline: An AI Observability Framework for Your Agentic Applications
articles.blurb: AWS authors propose an observability framework for agentic applications that crosses four layers with three concerns: reliability, cost, and security. They recommend OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions and evaluation gates, arguing that agents rarely fail with errors and often return confident wrong answers.

articles.headline: The layer of your platform nobody owns
articles.blurb: Platform teams standardize nearly everything except the operating system under their clusters. Developers should use an immutable, API-managed OS such as Talos Linux, with declarative configuration and atomic upgrades, at the cost of losing interactive shell access.

articles.headline: 87% of the Anthropic power will come from gas and 11% from coal in 2028
articles.blurb: A case study estimates that Anthropic could emit 32 million metric tons of carbon dioxide in 2028. About 87% of its US power will come from gas and 11% from coal that year, with no direct renewable energy commitments in the US as of November.

articles.headline: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
articles.blurb: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use "advanced cryptographic tools" to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.

articles.headline: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
articles.blurb: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely, a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom, was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content.

articles.headline: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
articles.blurb: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

articles.headline: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
articles.blurb: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

articles.headline: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
articles.blurb: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

articles.headline: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
articles.blurb: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet's access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines.

articles.headline: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
articles.blurb: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

articles.headline: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
articles.blurb: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

articles.headline: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
articles.blurb: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

articles.headline: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
articles.blurb: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today's epic patch batch dwarfs September's record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.
